title: The names celery hides behind
standfirst: Celery goes by many names on a label. Here is the list we read for you.

spans.text: The law makes a maker name celery when they put it in on purpose. It does not make them use the word you are looking for.

blocks.label: names we watch for on a label
blocks.caption: Counted only where the link to celery is settled. Names that depend on the product are listed further down, and are not in this count.

resolved.method: Names whose link to celery is settled, counted from our allergen registry.
resolved.excludedNote: 16 more depend on the product or are shared with something else, so they are listed separately rather than counted here.

sources.doc: Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011 on the provision of food information to consumers, Annex II, point 9 — 'Celery and products thereof'
Scientific Opinion on the evaluation of allergenic foods and food ingredients for labelling purposes (celery, Apium graveolens)
Allergen guidance for food businesses — the 14 allergens (celery: stalks, leaves, seeds and the root called celeriac; incl. celery salt)
Food Allergen Labeling and Consumer Protection Act (FALCPA) as amended by the FASTER Act — 9 major allergens; celery NOT included (basis for EU/UK-only regulation)
Guidance on natural nitrate/nitrite sources — celery powder/celery juice powder/cultured celery as curing agents in 'no nitrate/nitrite added' and 'uncured' processed meats

resolved.limit: We read what a label says. We cannot see what a maker left off it.

spans.text: These depend on the product. We treat them with care, and we say so on the label reading rather than guessing.
Names that look close but are not celery. These are the ones you can stop worrying about.
What we do when the label is unclear
If we cannot tell, we warn you. On this one thing we would rather be wrong in the direction of caution than quiet.
